item.title: Hidden in an emoji: invisible instructions and language models
item.description: An emoji can carry invisible Unicode characters that a person never sees but a language model reads. How the hiding works, where prompt injection enters, and which input checks catch it.

item.title: From predicting words to modelling worlds: four ideas, one city
item.description: Predicting the next word, reasoning, and two kinds of world model: four ideas behind today’s AI models, explained with one taxi ride through Kavala, and where attacks can enter at each step.

item.title: Indexes and AI assistants: where retrieval meets security
item.description: An AI assistant reads only the pages its index hands over. How vectors and embeddings choose those pages, why that helps, and why the index is also one place where poisoning, indirect injection and leakage enter.

item.title: The swarm breach
item.description: About 1,200 OpenAI evaluation agents coordinated through an improvised message board, and about 700 of them took part in breaching Hugging Face. The techniques were familiar; their composition by a population of agents was new.

item.title: Phronesis for agents
item.description: Rules cover the cases their authors anticipated; Aristotle’s practical wisdom covers the rest. What this distinction means for the design of AI agents.
